output.summary: KEP-783 proposes creating a new `k8s.io/component-base` repository as a generic toolkit of shared packages (ComponentConfig encoding/decoding and flag merging, command and flag building, common HTTPS status endpoints) for Kubernetes core components. The KEP is at status implementable, stage alpha.
output.rationale:
Core components each re-implement configuration, flag parsing, and status endpoints, and adopting ComponentConfig is hard. The KEP proposes a shared repo so components can adopt these pieces consistently, while avoiding moving code into k8s.io/apiserver that does not belong to an etcd-based apiserver. The work is incremental, starting with basics every component must handle such as configuration and flag parsing.</rationale>
<parameter name="outcome_reason">null

alternatives.option: Move the shared code into k8s.io/apiserver
alternatives.why_not: The goals say to avoid moving code into _k8s.io/apiserver_ which does not strictly belong to an etcd-based, API group-serving apiserver.

alternatives.option: Build a generic cloud-native component framework
alternatives.why_not: Non-goals state the library is not meant to be a generic cloud-native component builder; such a framework, if created, could consume these packages instead.

alternatives.option: Fix all problems in core components in one pass
alternatives.why_not: Non-goals say the work proceeds incrementally and avoids expanding beyond what is necessary.

evidence.quote: Avoid moving code into _k8s.io/apiserver_ which does not strictly belong to an etcd-based, API group-serving apiserver.
This repo will host a set of packages needed by the core components in a generic manner, like a **generic toolkit**.
Instead we'll work incrementally, and start with breaking out some basic stuff we _know_ every component must handle (e.g. configuration and flag parsing)
